pages.text: Cock-a-doodle-doo! The rooster crowed. Taro lay face down and closed his eyes again. "Just a little longer..." Morning sunlight slipped through the door.
The rooster crowed again. "I promised to go to the stream with Mumu... just a little longer." Taro rolled around, then fell asleep again.
When he opened his eyes, the room was bright. Taro jumped up. Outside, chickens were moving into the shade. "Oh? Is it that late already?"
Taro reached the well tree. Sharp-eared deer Mumu stood alone. Their long shadow had shortened into a round patch at their feet. "All the grown-ups went for their naps," Mumu said.
"We can't go to the stream now..." Taro's long tail drooped. Mumu bounded down beside him. "Tomorrow, get up as soon as the rooster crows."
"Stretch your arms and legs when you open your eyes. Sleepiness slips away." Mumu stretched their legs; Taro stretched his arms, refreshing his shoulders. Mumu sang, "Cock-a-Doodle-Doo—Jump Up!"
"Then splash basin water on your face!" Mumu pretended to splash. Taro copied and giggled. "I'll jump up tomorrow!"
The next day, cock-a-doodle-doo! Taro jumped up from bed. Stretching his arms and legs sent sleepiness away. "Cock-a-Doodle-Doo—Jump Up!"
Under the well tree, Taro tapped with a branch. Tok-tok, tok-tok. "One, jump up when I hear the rooster! Two, stretch arms and legs! Three, splash my face!" Mumu's shadow was still long.

Mumu bounded over, hugged Taro to their chest, and rested their chin on his shoulder. Getting up early made the day this much longer. "Cock-a-Doodle-Doo—Jump Up! Let's go to the stream!" Taro pulled Mumu's hand.
